name: TAMBO
summary: A proposed deep-valley observatory in the Peruvian Andes targets a clean sample of high-energy tau neutrinos using mountains as the interaction target.
physics_targets: Astrophysical tau-neutrino spectrum from approximately 1–100 PeV
detection_principle: Tau neutrinos interact in one mountain wall, and emerging tau leptons decay into air showers across the valley. An array of particle detectors on the opposite slope would sample those showers.

status.label: Research and development
status.evidence: Primary Peruvian institutions describe TAMBO as proposed and in early prototype development.

timeline.event: Valley-detector concept and sensitivity studies developed.
Peruvian partners describe early prototype development; full operation remains future.

collaboration.name: TAMBO Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Detector concept
key_parameters.value: Several thousand small water-Cherenkov or plastic-scintillator stations; evolving design

results.summary: Sensitivity and tau-flavour purity are evaluated in simulations; site engagement and prototype work precede the full observatory.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
